edges.mechanism: Developmental toxicity is the critical endpoint for the boron UL (rat NOAEL 9.6 mg B/kg/day). Higher maternal serum boron is associated with smaller newborns. EFSA excluded pregnant and lactating women from its calcium fructoborate approval.
edges.evidence: Animal developmental toxicity, one observational birth cohort, and regulatory exclusion. Human occupational data are reassuring. Avoid supplemental boron beyond diet.

edges.mechanism: EFSA excluded lactating women from its calcium fructoborate approval. The IOM UL (20 mg/day) still applies.
edges.evidence: Regulatory precaution; no human outcome data.

edges.mechanism: Boron is cleared almost entirely by the kidneys, unchanged (half-life about 21 h). Serum boron is above control levels before haemodialysis, and boron is readily dialysable. Accumulation is expected when GFR is reduced.
edges.evidence: Pharmacokinetic studies and small haemodialysis cohorts; no supplementation trials in CKD.

edges.mechanism: Boron supplementation shifted serum estradiol and testosterone and lowered SHBG in small human studies. This may matter for estrogen- or androgen-sensitive tumours. Observational data link higher dietary boron with lower prostate and lung cancer risk, so the direction of any clinical effect is unknown.
edges.evidence: Theoretical; based on small metabolic and uncontrolled hormone studies. No outcome data.

edges.mechanism: Boron raised serum 17beta-estradiol in postmenopausal women. Boron deprivation blunted the estradiol and copper rise in women on estrogen therapy. Additive estrogenic exposure is possible.
edges.evidence: Metabolic-ward studies, n of about 12-14; clinical significance unknown (very low certainty).

edges.mechanism: An uncontrolled 1-week study of 10 mg/day reported lower SHBG and higher free testosterone. A 7-week placebo-controlled trial at 2.5 mg/day found no effect.
edges.evidence: Conflicting very small studies; theoretical additive effect only.

edges.mechanism: Boron reduced urinary magnesium and calcium loss, more so on a low-Mg diet. Boron's effect on calcium excretion depended on Mg status. Combined Mg plus boron improved bone markers more than either alone in ovariectomised rats.
edges.evidence: Small human metabolic-ward studies (one found no modification of Mg-deprivation effects) plus animal data; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: 25(OH)D rose after 1 week of 10 mg/day boron. Boron improved Ca/Mg/P balance in vitamin D-deficient rats. This suggests a possible complementary effect on vitamin D-dependent mineral metabolism.
edges.evidence: One uncontrolled study (n=8) plus rat data; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Boron reduced urinary calcium excretion in postmenopausal women on low-Mg diets. Calcium fructoborate supplies a small amount of calcium (about 4.7% by weight).
edges.evidence: Small metabolic-ward studies; direction depended on Mg status.

edges.with: boron-containing products (stacked supplements, high-boron mineral water)
edges.mechanism: Boron from multiple sources adds up. The IOM UL is 20 mg/day for adults, lower for children; the EFSA ADI is 0.16 mg/kg bw/day. Accidental poisoning from a dietary supplement has been reported.
edges.evidence: Regulatory upper limits and case reports.

edges.mechanism: Oral ingestion of boric acid in gram quantities causes GI toxicity, and fatalities have occurred. Boric acid products are not for oral use.
ULs are much lower in children (3 mg at 1-3 y, 6 mg at 4-8 y, 11 mg at 9-13 y); no UL was set for infants. Paediatric boric acid ingestion is a recognised hazard.
edges.evidence: Official ULs (extrapolated by body weight) and case report.

edges.mechanism: Boron causes dose-dependent testicular toxicity in rats, mice and dogs (rat NOAEL 17.5 mg B/kg/day). Highly exposed human workers showed no reproductive effects.
edges.evidence: Animal toxicology; human occupational studies negative. Relevant only at doses well above the UL.

edges.mechanism: Plasma or blood boron (ICP-MS/ICP-OES) rises with supplementation and confirms exposure in suspected toxicity. Correlation with symptoms is uncertain.
edges.evidence: Case report and cohort/biomonitoring data; this is monitoring, not assay interference.
